hero.introParagraph: TeleDirectMD provides pediatric asthma and allergic rhinitis refills (ICD-10 J45.909 asthma, J30.9 allergic rhinitis) by secure video visit for children ages 5 to 17 with an established, stable diagnosis. TeleDirectMD is a physician-owned, MD-only telehealth practice operating in 41 states plus Washington, DC, and no nurse practitioners or physician assistants treat children here. A parent or legal guardian must be present and provide consent for every visit. This is a refill service only: TeleDirectMD does not diagnose new asthma, perform spirometry, reclassify severity, prescribe oral steroids without in-person follow-up, or prescribe biologics. Self-pay visits are $79, and TeleDirectMD does not prescribe controlled substances.

telehealthRegulations.sectionTitle: Telehealth Regulations Across Our Licensed States
paragraphs: TeleDirectMD operates only where its physicians hold active licensure, currently 41 states plus Washington, DC. Each state sets its own telemedicine standards, and in every state a parent or legal guardian must consent to a minor's care. TeleDirectMD verifies that the child is physically located in a licensed state at the time of the visit; care is not provided to children outside the licensed footprint.

Some states have additional requirements for telehealth refills of inhaled corticosteroids and controller medications for pediatric asthma. State-specific pages, such as our Delaware pages, cite the controlling state statute. TeleDirectMD does not prescribe controlled substances.

whatIsCondition.sectionTitle: What Is Asthma & Allergic Rhinitis Refills in Children?
paragraphs: This service provides refills only of established maintenance and rescue medications for children with a previously diagnosed and stable asthma or allergic rhinitis (hay fever). Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease; allergic rhinitis is allergy-driven inflammation of the nasal lining.

The NHLBI 2020 Focused Updates to the Asthma Management Guidelines and the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) reports provide the evidence base for maintenance therapy in children. TeleDirectMD does not make new asthma diagnoses, reclassify severity, or manage acute exacerbations online.

TeleDirectMD focuses on refills for stable, established diagnoses in children ages 5 to 17, with a parent present, and refers new or suspected asthma, acute attacks, and poor control to in-person or emergency care.

causesAndRiskFactors.sectionTitle: Causes and Risk Factors in Children
causesAndRiskFactors.intro: Pediatric asthma and allergic rhinitis in children ages 5 to 17 has several recognized causes and contributors:

items.label: Asthma triggers:
items.text: airway inflammation and hyperreactivity triggered by viruses, allergens, exercise, cold air, or smoke.

items.label: Allergic rhinitis:
items.text: an IgE-mediated response to pollen, dust mites, mold, or animal dander.

items.label: Family history (the atopic march):
items.text: a family history of asthma, eczema, or allergies increases risk.

items.label: Environmental exposures:
items.text: environmental tobacco smoke and air pollution worsen control.

causesAndRiskFactors.closing: Several conditions can mimic asthma and allergic rhinitis, including viral upper respiratory infections, vocal cord dysfunction, and pneumonia or bronchiolitis. TeleDirectMD uses history and video exam to confirm a stable, established diagnosis before refilling, and directs new, atypical, or worsening presentations to in-person evaluation.

differentialDiagnosis.sectionTitle: Differential Diagnosis: Asthma & Allergic Rhinitis vs Other Conditions
differentialDiagnosis.intro: Several conditions can mimic pediatric asthma and allergic rhinitis. TeleDirectMD physicians distinguish them by history and video exam before refilling.

telehealthAppropriate.title: Sometimes Appropriate for a Telehealth Refill
items: Asthma: recurrent reversible wheeze or cough with a prior clinician diagnosis, currently stable
Allergic rhinitis: sneezing, clear rhinorrhea, itchy eyes, and a seasonal pattern, currently stable
Review of current control, rescue-inhaler use, and inhaler technique
Refill of a known, stable maintenance and rescue regimen
Counseling on the montelukast boxed warning and trigger avoidance

requiresInPerson.title: Often Requires In-Person Evaluation
items: New or suspected (undiagnosed) asthma, which needs spirometry and an exam
Acute asthma attacks or exacerbations, which need urgent or emergency care
Vocal cord dysfunction, with throat tightness and stridor, often exercise-related
Pneumonia or bronchiolitis, with fever, focal findings, or distress
Children under age 5, who are not treated at TeleDirectMD for any condition

compareCards.title: Asthma vs Viral Upper Respiratory Infection
compareCards.text: Asthma is a chronic, recurrent, reversible pattern of wheeze and cough with a prior clinician diagnosis. A viral upper respiratory infection produces self-limited cold symptoms without a chronic pattern. TeleDirectMD refills established, stable asthma but does not diagnose new asthma or treat acute respiratory illness that requires a hands-on exam.

compareCards.title: Allergic Rhinitis vs Vocal Cord Dysfunction
compareCards.text: Allergic rhinitis features sneezing, clear rhinorrhea, itchy eyes, and a seasonal pattern. Vocal cord dysfunction causes throat tightness and stridor, often exercise-related, and needs specialist evaluation. Pneumonia or bronchiolitis presents with fever, focal findings, and distress requiring in-person or emergency care.

differentialDiagnosis.closing: If the diagnosis is new, unstable, or worsening, or there are red-flag features, TeleDirectMD will direct you to in-person or emergency care rather than refilling medications by video.

treatmentOptions.intro: A TeleDirectMD physician reviews the child's existing diagnosis, current regimen, control, and technique, then refills appropriate maintenance and rescue medications. Poorly controlled children are referred for in-person reassessment rather than simply re-supplied. Montelukast prescribing follows the DailyMed montelukast labeling and the FDA 2020 boxed warning, and is reserved for allergic rhinitis when other therapies are inadequate or not tolerated.

sections.title: Maintenance controllers
sections.text: Inhaled corticosteroids such as fluticasone HFA (FDA-labeled for ages 4 and older) are refilled for established asthma. Controllers should not be stopped when the child feels well; refill before they run out. Review inhaler technique and spacer use at each visit.

sections.title: Rescue medication
sections.text: Albuterol HFA rescue inhalers (FDA-labeled for ages 4 and older for most products) are refilled for established asthma. Needing a rescue inhaler more than twice a week signals poor control and prompts referral for in-person reassessment rather than a simple refill.

sections.title: Allergic rhinitis therapy
sections.text: Intranasal steroids such as fluticasone (Flonase, ages 4 and older) and mometasone (Nasonex, ages 2 and older), oral antihistamines, and montelukast may be refilled. Per the FDA 2020 boxed warning, montelukast is reserved for allergic rhinitis when other therapies are inadequate or not tolerated, with counseling about neuropsychiatric risks.

sections.title: When escalation is needed
sections.text: Poor control may signal the need for a step-up in therapy, technique review, or spirometry that telehealth refills cannot safely provide. Children needing escalation, oral steroids, biologics, or severity reclassification are referred to their pediatrician or pulmonologist.

homeCare.sectionTitle: Home Care, Recovery Timeline, Prevention, and Follow-up

whatToDoNow.title: Timeline and What to Do Now
items: Keep an up-to-date written asthma action plan from the child's regular clinician.
Use a spacer with metered-dose inhalers and review technique regularly.
Refill controllers before they run out; do not stop maintenance therapy when feeling well.
Reduce triggers such as tobacco smoke, dust mites, and known allergens.

whatToWatch.title: What to Watch For
items: Track rescue-inhaler use; needing it more than twice a week signals poor control.
Watch for night-time awakenings from cough or wheeze, which signal poor control.
Seek in-person or emergency care for any severe breathing difficulty.
Call 911 for severe shortness of breath, inability to speak in full sentences, or blue lips.

followUp.title: Prevention and Follow-up
items: Refill controllers and rescue inhalers before they run out to avoid gaps in therapy.
Continue trigger reduction at home, including reducing tobacco smoke and allergen exposure.
Return for in-person reassessment if control worsens or rescue use increases.
Keep regular follow-up with the child's pediatrician or pulmonologist for ongoing chronic-disease management.
Counsel on the montelukast boxed warning and report any mood or behavior changes promptly.

faq.sectionTitle: Pediatric Asthma & Allergic Rhinitis Refills FAQs

items.question: Can TeleDirectMD refill my child's asthma inhaler online?
items.answer: Yes, for established diagnoses. TeleDirectMD refills asthma and allergic rhinitis medications (ICD-10 J45.909 and J30.9) by video for children ages 5 to 17 who already have a documented, stable diagnosis and a parent present. An MD reviews the diagnosis, current control, and technique before refilling. The self-pay visit is $79, available in 41 states plus Washington, DC. TeleDirectMD does not diagnose new asthma.

items.question: Will TeleDirectMD diagnose new asthma in my child?
items.answer: No. TeleDirectMD provides refills only for children ages 5 to 17 with an existing, documented asthma diagnosis; it does not make new asthma diagnoses, perform spirometry, or reclassify severity online. New or suspected asthma requires in-person evaluation and lung-function testing. Children needing a first diagnosis are referred to their pediatrician or a pulmonologist rather than started on controller therapy by video.

items.question: What asthma and allergy medications can TeleDirectMD refill for a child?
items.answer: For children ages 5 to 17 with an established diagnosis, TeleDirectMD can refill albuterol HFA rescue inhalers (ages 4+), inhaled fluticasone controllers (ages 4+), montelukast, and nasal sprays such as fluticasone (Flonase, ages 4+) and mometasone (Nasonex, ages 2+), plus antihistamines. Per the FDA 2020 boxed warning, montelukast for allergic rhinitis is reserved for children who cannot tolerate or respond to other therapies.

items.question: What is the montelukast (Singulair) boxed warning TeleDirectMD counsels about?
items.answer: The FDA added a boxed warning in 2020 about serious mental-health side effects of montelukast, including agitation, depression, and suicidal thoughts or actions. TeleDirectMD physicians counsel parents of children ages 5 to 17 about this risk and, for allergic rhinitis, reserve montelukast for children who do not respond to or cannot tolerate other allergy medicines, consistent with the FDA recommendation.

items.question: Can TeleDirectMD treat an asthma attack online?
items.answer: No. TeleDirectMD does not manage acute asthma attacks or exacerbations online for any child. A child ages 5 to 17 with severe shortness of breath, inability to speak in full sentences, or blue lips needs emergency care, call 911. This service is limited to refills of maintenance and rescue medications for stable, established asthma; acute worsening requires in-person or emergency evaluation.

items.question: Does a parent need to be present for an asthma refill visit?
items.answer: Yes. A parent or legal guardian must be present for the entire visit and provide consent for any child ages 5 to 17 seen by TeleDirectMD for an asthma or allergy refill. The guardian's identity is verified, and the child must be physically located in one of the 41 states plus Washington, DC where TeleDirectMD is licensed at the time of the visit.

items.question: What if my child's asthma is poorly controlled?
items.answer: If a child ages 5 to 17 is using a rescue inhaler more than twice a week, waking at night from symptoms, or having frequent flares, TeleDirectMD refers for in-person reassessment rather than simply re-supplying the same regimen. Poor control may signal the need for a step-up in therapy, technique review, or spirometry that telehealth refills cannot safely provide.

items.question: How much does an online pediatric asthma refill visit cost?
items.answer: An online pediatric asthma and allergic rhinitis refill visit at TeleDirectMD costs $79 self-pay, no insurance required, for children ages 5 to 17 with an established diagnosis. TeleDirectMD is in-network with Aetna, select Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, and UnitedHealthcare where applicable, but not in-network with any Medicaid, Managed Medicaid, CHIP, or Medicare-Medicaid plan in any state.

items.question: Will TeleDirectMD prescribe oral steroids for my child's asthma?
items.answer: No. TeleDirectMD does not prescribe oral or systemic corticosteroids for children ages 5 to 17 without in-person follow-up, and it does not prescribe biologics. A child whose asthma is severe enough to need an oral steroid burst is experiencing an exacerbation that warrants in-person or emergency evaluation. This refill service is limited to maintenance inhalers, montelukast, nasal sprays, and antihistamines.

items.question: Can TeleDirectMD refill allergic rhinitis (hay fever) medications too?
items.answer: Yes. TeleDirectMD refills allergic rhinitis medications (ICD-10 J30.9) for children ages 5 to 17 with an established diagnosis, including intranasal steroids such as fluticasone (ages 4+) and mometasone (ages 2+), oral antihistamines, and montelukast. Per the FDA 2020 boxed warning, montelukast is reserved for allergic rhinitis when other therapies are inadequate or not tolerated, with counseling about neuropsychiatric risks.

paragraphs: This page is informational and is not a substitute for in-person medical care. TeleDirectMD provides asthma and allergic rhinitis refills for children ages 5 to 17 with an established diagnosis; we do not treat children under age 5 for any condition (ages 0 to 4 are excluded). A parent or legal guardian must be present for the entire visit and provide consent, and the child must be physically located in a licensed state (41 states plus Washington, DC) at the time of the visit.

TeleDirectMD does not prescribe controlled substances or isotretinoin, does not diagnose or treat mental health conditions or ADHD, and does not make new asthma diagnoses. It does not perform spirometry, reclassify severity, manage acute exacerbations, prescribe oral or systemic steroids without in-person follow-up, or prescribe biologics. Any infant under 3 months with fever requires emergency care. TeleDirectMD is not in-network with any Medicaid, Managed Medicaid, CHIP, or Medicare-Medicaid plan in any state.
